title: Jianzhen's voyage to Japan
summary: After five failed attempts, the Chinese Vinaya master Jianzhen (Ganjin) left Yangzhou in late 753 aboard a Japanese embassy ship, crossed by way of Okinawa and Yakushima, landed in southern Kyushu, and reached the capital Nara in early 754, where he went on to teach the Buddhist precepts, first at Tōdaiji and then at Tōshōdai-ji.

uncertainty.note: Bingenheimer converts the Chinese and Japanese calendar dates of the Tōdaiwajō tōseiden to Western dates and warns they may be off by a day or two; he gives Yangzhou departure as 28 Nov. 753. Other pages give 20 December 753 for the Kagoshima landing (yesyakushima) or only 'autumn 753' and 'spring 754'. The twelfth-month events of Tianbao 12 fall in January 754 by his conversion (6th day = 4 Jan. 754).

importance.justification: A documented sixth-attempt sea crossing that brought a Chinese Vinaya master and his party to Japan's court, where he helped establish monastic ordination.

beats.caption: Jianzhen boards the Japanese vice-envoy's ship at Yangzhou, after five earlier attempts failed, and four ships set out together.
After Okinawa the second ship reaches Yakushima, then a port in Satsuma in southwest Kyushu, and Jianzhen is taken to Dazaifu.
Jianzhen is welcomed into Nara and lodged at Tōdaiji, which brought Chinese Vinaya teaching to Japan's court.

reviewer_note: Least sure: Western dates are the translator's conversions (one or two days of slack); another page gives 20 December 753 for the landing. Okinawa is plotted at the island's Wikidata point; Aernaibodao is the translator's gloss. Naniwa is plotted at Osaka. Wikidata points are city or island centres, so kilometres of slack.
